title: e-Invoicing mandates and updates: Sweden
summary: Stay on top of the latest news regarding e-Invoicing mandates in Sweden including specifications, technical information and new deadlines.
body_markdown:
## **October 2026**


Sweden has now taken a significant step toward determining how ViDA—and potentially broader domestic e-Invoicing requirements—will be implemented.


In February 2026, the Swedish government launched a formal inquiry into the changes needed to implement ViDA’s digital reporting and e-Invoicing requirements in Swedish law. Significantly, the inquiry will also assess whether Sweden should introduce mandatory e-Invoicing and digital reporting for domestic transactions.


For now, there is still **no domestic B2B e-Invoicing mandate** in Sweden. The inquiry is ongoing, with its findings due by **November 30, 2027** .


Meanwhile, Swedish businesses involved in relevant cross-border B2B transactions within the EU will need to prepare for ViDA requirements taking effect on **July 1, 2030** . These requirements will introduce mandatory e-Invoicing and near-real-time digital reporting for applicable transactions.


## **March 2025**


The EU has formally adopted its VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) package, bringing greater clarity to the future of e-Invoicing in Sweden and across the European Union.


Under ViDA, e-Invoicing and digital reporting will become mandatory for relevant cross-border B2B transactions within the EU from July 1, 2030. EU Member States will also have greater flexibility to introduce mandatory e-Invoicing for domestic transactions.


For Sweden, this means changes to national legislation will be required ahead of the 2030 deadline. However, Sweden has not yet introduced a domestic B2B e-Invoicing mandate. E-Invoicing requirements continue to apply primarily to public procurement, while B2B e-Invoicing remains voluntary.


The adoption of ViDA nevertheless marks an important milestone for Swedish businesses. Organizations should begin considering how their invoicing processes and technology will support structured e-Invoices and digital reporting as the new EU framework takes shape.


## February 2023


Sweden set to adopt mandatory e-Invoicing in line with the ViDA proposal


The Swedish authorities are the first to demonstrate compliance of the proposals laid out in the[ViDA report](https://blogs.opentext.com/e-invoicing-mandates-the-european-union/) . They have submitted a request to implement B2B and B2G e-invoicing and e-Reporting, in compliance with the policy options described by the ViDA.


No timeline has been published or indicated so far for the implementation of e-invoicing.


For more information on this initiative, see the announcement from the Swedish Agency for Digital Government[here](https://www.digg.se/download/18.5b30ce7218475cd9ed315efb/1675860922174/hemstallan-e-faktura.pdf) .
